correctness.rationale: The path grading gives the derived ideal L₂=U⊗V ⊕ V⊗W ⊕ U⊗V⊗W and L₃=U⊗V⊗W because all basis paths of lengths two and three occur as single brackets. The derived ideal is abelian, and bracketing x=u+v+w+z with U⊗V and with V⊗W independently tests w and u, respectively, against a fixed nonzero simple tensor. Each test is injective in that endpoint variable over every field. The resulting centralizer is V⊕L₂. Once s is fixed by its quotient dimension, the first and third layer dimensions give the integer sum and product of the outer multiplicities. Path reversal is an anti-isomorphism and its negative is a Lie isomorphism, including in characteristic two. The two families both give graded dimensions (14h,48h²,72h³) and have centralizer quotient dimensions 6h and 8h. The frozen checker and its stated bounded scope were inspected, not executed; the reconstruction proves the uniform statement.

evidence: The prior third commutator equation is a⊗v′−a′⊗v+u⊗c′−u′⊗c=0. For Y in [L,L], a′=b′=c′=0, so it becomes a⊗v′−u′⊗c=0 for arbitrary u′ and v′. Testing each separately forces a=c=0, and the two other equations are automatic. These path equations, and the identification of [L,L] with the paths of lengths at least two, hold without a finite-field assumption. This gives the exact centralizer, quotient dimension and isomorphism criterion with reversal.

There is also a numerical implication of the actual polynomial, not merely of the existence of a commuting-pair invariant. Write X=r+t. The common graded dimensions determine {s,X} from s+X and sX, and determine W=2rst and D=2sX. The only possible ambiguity switches s and X, with both at least two. Put M=max(s,X) and m=min(s,X) in that case. After removing q^{W+D}, the prior sum's zero-middle-rank part has highest exponent strictly below 2X: each product N_r(i)N_t(j) has degree ≤2X and each nonzero rank pair has a positive E(i,j). Its rank-one-middle part has degree at most s+X, since the outer-rank contributions in braces have exponents strictly below X after removal of q^D. Its rank-two-middle term has degree 2s. Consequently only the candidate with larger middle parameter M has degree 2M. The leading terms of nonzero rank summands have positive coefficients. This distinguishes the proposed collisions for all h, and every case of this ambiguity, as polynomials.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: An isomorphism over a finite field would give equal counts over all extensions of that field, so these different polynomials rule it out. The same obstruction extends to any field by putting the entries of a hypothetical isomorphism and its inverse determinant in a finitely generated ring over Z and specializing at a maximal ideal with finite residue field; the path structure constants are integral. More directly, the prior commutator equations make the centralizer formula an immediate calculation over the original field. Thus even the all-field scope does not separate the centralizer-based rigidity from what the earlier explicit result yields.

originality.rationale: The earlier same-family commuting-pair result gives explicit equations for the full commutator. Restricting its primed variable to the derived ideal gives the centralizer by direct substitution and tensor injectivity, with no new lemma about the family required. Separately, the published polynomial formula together with the three graded dimensions already distinguishes all candidate triples up to outer reversal, not just the h=1 example. The exact collision tuples are not claimed to have appeared previously; their dimension comparison and distinction are substitutions into the same prior data. This is established prior implication, not an access problem or a claim the mathematics is false.
